lines.before: Never raise a limit to make a run pass. Keep a margin larger than CI's build-to-build drift. Why: a budget that bends on request is not a budget. <!-- PROJECT ADAPTER A12 -->
lines.after: Never raise a limit to make a run pass. Why: a budget that bends on request is not a budget, and an ask the rule did not mean teaches people to wave asks through. <!-- PROJECT ADAPTER A12 -->

lines.before: **One request, two checks (planned work).** A plan that grows a budget asks once, at approval: per line, the estimate + max(10%, the drift floor), landed in one commit. One final check at the PR's last gate, after review fixes: over -> steps 1-3; more room than the margin -> lower to measured + margin. A measurement above the estimate before the raise lands re-sends the request. Why: size stays a decision without a stop per commit, and padding never accumulates.
lines.after: - **One request per plan, from a measurement.** Build a first version, measure, then ask once per line at plan approval: the measured growth plus a margin of 10% of it. Never ask from an estimate; a count line (files, not bytes) is asked exactly.
lines.why: the ask is made from a measurement, not an estimate, and the drift floor is retired where measuring builds are identical; the end check is its own bullet
